messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 [AUTO] Unusual auth-rate spike detected on auth-api from multiple foreign IPs. 403/401 surges observed, +540% vs baseline in last 10m. Pager: oncall-sre. Runbook: suspicious-auth. thread_ts=1743001234
Sam (oncall-sre): I'm on it. grabbing logs now. can someone check if any recently rotated keys were uploaded to public buckets?
Marta (support): getting customer reports of token failures - several customers reporting 401s for service tokens. ticket #INC-9042 created.
Noah (security): @Sam do not rotate anything yet until we confirm scope. prioritize containment: block the offending IPs at edge, throttle auth endpoint, disable any exposed service keys.
Priya (eng-infra): Applying WAF block for the offending CIDRs now: `aws wafv2 update-web-acl --scope REGIONAL --id acl-xyz --rules ...` I'll paste exact rule in a sec.
Jules (api-owner): Confirmed spike originates from endpoints hitting `/v1/auth/token` with unusual user-agent `python-requests/2.28` and a couple of suspicious `x-forwarded-for` headers. Example log snippet (redacted): `2026-02-12T16:01:12Z auth-api request id=redacted ip=45.77.###.### user=service-account-abc status=401`
Sam (oncall-sre): Ok WAF rule deployed. Also enabling short-term rate-limit on `/v1/auth/token` to 5r/s per IP. Command: `kong rate-limiting set /v1/auth/token 5`
Noah (security): I'm pulling IAM logs and checking the KMS audit for any CreateKey/ImportKey activity. If keys were exported, we escalate to legal and CISO.
Priya (eng-infra): IAM logs show several `GetSecretValue` calls for `prod/service/stripe-key` from an IAM role that hasn't been used in 6 months. Source IPs match spike.
Jules (api-owner): Wait — that role was part of the legacy batch workers. Could be a leaked credential from archived infra. I'm disabling the role now: `aws iam update-assume-role-policy --role-name legacy-batch --policy-document '{}'`
Sam (oncall-sre): Disabling role applied. Rotating any long-lived access keys for `legacy-batch` next. Not rotating production customer keys yet; only rotating service keys tied to role.
Marta (support): Customer-facing status posted to status.redwood.ai: "Investigating auth disruptions affecting token issuance for some integrations." Adding impacted customers list.
Noah (security): I recommend immediate rotation of any access keys used by that role and a forced refresh for affected service tokens. Preparing scope doc. Also creating a preserved snapshot of logs for forensic analysis: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_function" AND jsonPayload.method="GetSecretValue"' > /tmp/forensic-1743001234.log`
Priya (eng-infra): Rotating keys for role `legacy-batch` now. Will create new role with least privilege and move consumers. Deploying HSM policy to block plaintext key exports.
Jules (api-owner): Quick note — can we check if any customer data was accessed? Secrets show read access but application logs don't show successful token exchanges for customer sessions.
Noah (security): Early indicators: secrets were requested, but no downstream calls to customer data endpoints were logged. Still treating as potential data exposure until forensics confirm.
Sam (oncall-sre): Handoff to Noah for 20-min deep-dive. I'm staying on the channel for infra actions. Starting incident call in 5m: zoom link https://zoom.redwood.ai/j/123456789 (incident bridge).
Marta (support): Sent targeted outbound notice to affected customers: brief, no PII, "We're investigating an authentication incident; recommended to rotate integration tokens once we confirm scope." Tiered notice ready for escalation.
Noah (security): Forensics note: saving `/tmp/forensic-1743001234.log` to secure evidence bucket `s3://rdw-forensics/1743001234/` with restricted ACLs. Also creating an internal timeline doc.
Priya (eng-infra): WAF blocks holding; auth-error rates dropping to +40% vs baseline. Rate limits appear to have blunted the surge.
Jules (api-owner): I ran a quick grep across app logs for signs of successful token redemption: none so far. Good sign.
Sam (oncall-sre): Plan for next hour: 1) complete key rotations for legacy role, 2) validate no customer-data API calls, 3) keep WAF block and rate limits until 8am UTC, 4) notify legal and exec if evidence of key exfiltration.
Noah (security): Legal looped in. If forensics show key material left our environment, we will need to follow breach notification cadence. For now marking as P2 and active.
Marta (support): Keeping status page updated. Will prepare CS template if we need to ask customers to rotate tokens.
Sam (oncall-sre): Leaving channel to get some rest; handoff to Noah at 1743001500. If anything critical, page me again.
Noah (security): Acknowledged handoff. Continuing investigation, will post update every 30m or on critical changes.
incident-bot: [UPDATE] Incident 1743001234 status changed to "Mitigating" by Sam.
Noah (security): 1743001899 — interim summary: WAF+rate-limit applied, compromised role disabled, keys rotated for legacy role, no confirmed customer-data access. Forensics snapshot stored. Keeping incident open for verification and root cause analysis. Next update +30m."
